newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BROKERS NEDEE, MIGNON IN COOPERATION TALKS.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BROKERS NEDEE, MIGNON IN COOPERATION TALKS.

text.p: Ghent-based Belgian brokerage Nedee & Cie is holding talks with Brussels-based brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerk (MHD) with a view to cooperation, spokesmen for the two companies said on Wednesday.
But they denied that Nedee, a 100-percent unit of Belgian Cera Bank, was about to take over Mignon.
"We have had talks about possible cooperation, but there are no plans to buy Mignon at this moment," Nedee's management committee chairman Franky Depickere told Reuters.
"One can say we are in talks to study a cooperation with Cera/Nedee," Mignon partner Daniel Mignon told Reuters.

"We aim to finalise our talks within three months. But that will not necessarily be with Cera. We are also talking to other potential partners," Mignon added, but declined to be specific. MHD partner Georges Hanart told Reuters MHD was also looking at other interested parties in Belgium, the U.K. and France.
Mignon, who controls 70 percent of MHD's capital, said that in light of the advent of the European single currency, his firm needed to broaden its capital base.
"We are very active in institutional brokerage, which is a business in which economies of scale are important. There is a tendency towards regrouping," he said.
Highly specialised MHD is also active in asset management for wealthy individuals and has developed a broad range of equity indices. MHD employs 15 people in its Brussels office.
Nedee is based in the western Belgian city of Ghent, where 65 of its 90 employees are based. It has several branches in the Flanders, the northern, Dutch-speaking part of Belgium.
"We have the ambition to expand and offer our services in the rest of Belgium," Nedee's Depickere said.
Nedee's presence in Brussels, the financial heart of Belgium, is limited to a two-man office. Sources close to the company said that Cera/Nedee want a more prominent place in Brussels.
Nedee is active in private banking, corporate finance, institutional brokerage and market making in equity derivatives.
A merger of the firms would still not put them in the same league as powerhouses Dewaay and Petercam, but further consolidate Nedee's position as a top 10 brokerage in Belgium.

For Cera Bank, a retail bank which focuses on the agricultural sector, a deal between its Nedee unit and Mignon would continue its recent expansion into financial market activities and strengthen its position in equities.
Cera, Belgium's sixth-largest bank, said in December it planned to buy 80 percent of Banque Indosuez Belgique from French Banque Indosuez. Indosuez Belgium is very active in fixed-income trading.
